title: Saudi Leader Is Said to Push Trump to Continue Iran War in Recent Calls
partialText: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman sees a “historic opportunity” to remake the region, according to people briefed by U.S. officials on the conversations.

title: Israel Plans to Control Large Parts of Southern Lebanon, Defense Minister Says
partialText: Israel Katz, the Israeli defense minister, suggested that Israeli troops might remain in parts of Lebanon even after the fighting there winds down.

title: College Graduates Are Facing the Grimmest Job Market in Years
partialText: Artificial intelligence could reshape work, but for now a low-hire, low-fire labor market is the main impediment for young people seeking employment.

title: Gregory Bovino’s Final Days: Harsh Words and Few Regrets
partialText: He was the face of the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown. But as he begins a retirement that was not entirely voluntary, the Border Patrol leader says he did not go far enough.

title: Supreme Court Hears Trump Request to Block Asylum Seekers
partialText: A policy of turning back many asylum seekers at the border was rescinded in 2021, but the Justice Department wants the flexibility to reinstate it as a tool for border control.

title: Stephen Miller Asks Why Texas Pays to Teach Undocumented Children
partialText: Citing gridlock in Washington, President Trump’s top immigration adviser encouraged Texas lawmakers to lead on conservative priorities.

title: Wicked Stepmother No Longer, a Female Pharoah Gets a Reputational Makeover
partialText: A reassessment of damaged 3,500-year-old statuary adds to evidence that Queen Hatshepsut wasn’t the villain that scholars long took her to be.

title: David A. Ross Sought Epstein’s Help to Build Art Museums. Now He’s Facing the Fallout.
partialText: He mastered the world of the “Epstein Class” to build great museums. Now he’s confronting the cost.

title: Thomas Massie Thinks Being Hated by Trump Is ‘Worth It.’ Will Voters Agree?
partialText: The Republican congressman from Kentucky is a die-hard libertarian who has centered his campaign on his willingness to buck the president. It has bought him the most expensive primary in the country.

title: Should You Need to Prove Citizenship to Vote? Ask Kansas.
partialText: A Kansas law required a passport, a birth certificate or other proof of citizenship to register, but it was struck down after a court found that around 31,000 eligible voters had been blocked.

title: Trump, Who Calls Mail-in Voting ‘Cheating,’ Just Voted by Mail
partialText: President Trump has long fixated on mail-in voting to bolster his baseless claims of widespread voter fraud. But he recently used the method in a Florida special election.

title: In Oklahoma, Alan Armstrong Will Fill Markwayne Mullin’s Senate Seat
partialText: Gov. Kevin Stitt selected Mr. Armstrong, a fellow Republican and an energy executive, to play a caretaker role in the seat until the next election.

title: Covid Relief Loans Are Haunting Small Businesses
partialText: The Small Business Administration lent $378 billion to keep businesses afloat. Getting paid back is proving difficult.

title: How Do You Measure Snow From Space? First, Climb a Mountain.
partialText: A new satellite could transform how water is studied worldwide. But to help unlock its capabilities, scientists first needed to take critical measurements on a mountaintop.

title: Reality TV Confronts a Harsh TV Reality
partialText: The number of unscripted series has plummeted by a third since 2022. As the industry rapidly changes, an era is quietly vanishing.

title: NASA Adds Moon Base and Nuclear-Powered Mars Spacecraft to Road Map
partialText: The agency announced the more specific plans and timelines after years of suggesting it may build a lunar outpost.

title: Comedy’s Most Manipulative Shot … and Its Greatest Weapon
partialText: Audience reactions are a staple of standup specials. But they’re a strange device when you take a closer look.

title: Why Are So Many Democrats So Far Out of Touch?
partialText: Candidates in safe districts are under no pressure to moderate in order to win.

title: What Happens if 20 Percent of the World’s Oil Disappears?
partialText: The war with Iran could change how the whole world thinks about energy security in the future. The energy policy expert Jason Bordoff explains.

title: Health Woes
partialText: We look into the turmoil at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

title: Afghanistan Frees American Dennis Coyle from Detention
partialText: Dennis Walter Coyle, a researcher from Colorado, had been held since last year by the Taliban government.

title: Chavez Revelations Force Teachers to Rethink How They Teach His Legacy
partialText: In classrooms across the country, educators are weighing whether to shift focus from Cesar Chavez to the broader labor movement he helped lead.

title: Government Cuts Gut the Memory of Argentina’s Dirty War
partialText: Fifty years after the military dictatorship, Argentina’s government is defunding human rights groups and promoting a revisionist account of the junta’s crimes.

title: In N.Y.C. Classes, Teachers Can Use A.I. to Plan but Not to Assign Grades
partialText: The largest school system in the United States released its first guide on how teachers can incorporate artificial intelligence into their work and schools.
